questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Only use it when you need to stop quickly.
Only use it on slippery roads.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe if you use it properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe if you use it properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection?

options.text: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so that oncoming drivers can see you as early as possible. For example, at a blind corner to your right, move to the left side of your lane so you are seen sooner.

questions.question: What should you see when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. The edge of your arm may show, but focus on the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually located on the left handgrip.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash compared to riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What should you do with a helmet after a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Replace it.
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been worn during a crash.

questions.question: How should you hold the handgrips on rough surfaces?

options.text: With lots of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly on rough surfaces to keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass quickly.
Do not weave between the cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between the cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. You may encounter opening doors or cars pulling into traffic. You will not have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder either.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only encourage them to tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
It guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will give you the right of way. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not see them.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do with their space cushion?

options.text: They should cut it in half.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should keep it adequate.
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right foot.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may slide.
The motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may slide.
The motorcycle may jerk and a warning light comes on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may slide.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear too fast, the motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may slide, causing you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than normal.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower, especially in curves and over bumps. The extra weight also means longer acceleration and stopping distances, so keep a larger space cushion.

questions.question: What should a proper lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you set up for turns
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually found?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: When a rear tire skids:

options.text: It only matters if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When you apply too much rear brake, the rear wheel locks up. Once locked, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face during a crash.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be worn with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire going flat. Tire problems are usually noticed by sudden changes in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You can go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must pass only in areas where it is safe and legal. You must obey the speed limit and complete the pass within the passing zone.

questions.question: When turning:

options.text: You have less grip for braking.
You have more grip for braking.
Braking works the same as on a straight road.
You should never brake while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less grip for braking.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When leaning to turn, some of your tire grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for braking.
